Data Preparation

Enter text here.

## Writing make_dataset() Function ##
def make_dataset(df):
  """
  The make_dataset() function...
  Output: DataSet object; Converted DataFrame into DataSet object.
  --
  Parameters:
  - df: DataFrame object; DataFrame to be converted into DataSet.
  """
  ## Remove Stopwords from Title and Text ##
  stop = stopwords.words('english')
  # Remove from title
  df["title"] = df['title'].apply(lambda x: ' '.join([word for word in x.split() if word not in (stop)]))
  df["text"] = df['text'].apply(lambda x: ' '.join([word for word in x.split() if word not in (stop)]))

  ## Converting into DataSet Object ##
  # Main conversion.
  ds = tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices(
    (
        {
            "title" : df[["title"]],
            "text" : df[["text"]]
        },
        {
            "fake" : df[["fake"]]
        }
    )
  )
  # Batching DataSet.
  ds.batch(100)

  return ds

Train/Test/Validation Split

Enter text here.

## Reading Data as DataSet ##
articles_ds = make_dataset(articles)
articles_ds = articles_ds.shuffle(buffer_size = len(articles_ds), reshuffle_each_iteration=False)
## Train/Test/Validation Split ##
train_size = int(0.7*len(articles_ds))
val_size   = int(0.2*len(articles_ds))

# Training data
train = articles_ds.take(train_size).batch(20)
# Validation data
val = articles_ds.skip(train_size).take(val_size).batch(20)
# Test data
test = articles_ds.skip(train_size + val_size).batch(20)

Text Vectorization

Apply the following text vectorization script to make the data more usable for the models.

#preparing a text vectorization layer for tf model
size_vocabulary = 2000

def standardization(input_data):
    lowercase = tf.strings.lower(input_data)
    no_punctuation = tf.strings.regex_replace(lowercase,
                                  '[%s]' % re.escape(string.punctuation),'')
    return no_punctuation

title_vectorize_layer = TextVectorization(
    standardize=standardization,
    max_tokens=size_vocabulary, # only consider this many words
    output_mode='int',
    output_sequence_length=500)

title_vectorize_layer.adapt(train.map(lambda x, y: x["title"]))

Creating Models

With the given data, we will try to answer the following question.

When detecting fake news, is it most effective to focus on only the title of the article, the full text of the article, or both?

To address this question, construct the models for each case.

Title Only Model

## Building Model from Sequential ##
# Only the top x amount of words will be tracked
max_tokens = 2000

# Model
model = tf.keras.Sequential([
  # layers.Embedding(max_tokens, output_dim = 3, name="embedding"),
  # layers.Dropout(0.2),
  layers.GlobalAveragePooling1D(),
  layers.Dropout(0.2),
  layers.Dense(len(articles["fake"]))]
)
## Including Loss Function ##
model.compile(loss=losses.SparseCategoricalCrossentropy(from_logits=True),
              optimizer='adam',
              metrics=['accuracy'])
## Running Model ##
history = model.fit(train, epochs = 10, validation_data = val)
